rows.subtype: Child fetches the teacher and a bandage [Actor]
rows.description: A child sees the same fall, feels sorry, and calmly goes to fetch help; concern with a steady body leads to action instead of shared panic.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.subtype: Overwhelmed by a friend's crisis, then withdrawing [Actor]
rows.description: A teenager absorbs a friend's grief, sleeps badly, and starts avoiding the friend out of exhaustion; too much feeling-with can end in pulling away from the one who needs them.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
related mind states: grief, tiredness, detachment, overwhelm

rows.subtype: Caring role wears the carer down [Actor]
rows.description: A nursing or counselling student feels every patient's pain, grows numb and irritable, and wonders if they care less; this is fatigue from over-feeling, not a lack of heart.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 23–26
related mind states: curiosity, tiredness, detachment, awe

rows.description: An adult takes slow breaths, feels warm concern rather than merging with the pain, asks "what would help?", and looks after their own rest so care can last.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17, 18–22

rows.description: A supervisor sees a caregiver grow hard or tearful after too many hard cases and arranges rest, talk and shared load; caring people need care too.

rows.subtype: Adult offers words to a child [Observer]
rows.description: A parent or teacher says "your face looks cross, are you upset?" to help a child name what they feel; simple naming without pressure builds emotional vocabulary.

rows.subtype: Feels something but cannot name it [Actor]
rows.description: A child says "I feel weird" and points to a tight stomach when asked; the feeling is real, but finding the words for it is difficult.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager answers every question about mood with "fine" or "nothing", and describes bodily aches more than feelings; they are not cold, they lack the map of words.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A person in a close relationship feels the other never says what they feel and takes it as coldness; it may be difficulty naming feelings, not a lack of caring.

rows.subtype: Learning words for feelings with support [Response]
rows.description: An adult builds a list of feeling words, notices bodily cues such as a tight chest, writes daily notes, and speaks to a counsellor if the difficulty causes distress in work or love.
